finding: The footer promises "Every publish is restorable" on the one surface a user consults before rolling back; the product retains only the newest 20 publish payloads and nulls the rest.
evidence: 949:4474 footer text fetched: "Every publish is restorable. Rolling back redeploys that version." Code: server/services/publish.service.ts:436 `const PUBLISH_HISTORY_RETAINED = 20;` and :459 "Prune: null the payload on COMPLETED jobs older than the 20 most recent". Sibling board 1704:8309 states the true rule: "you can roll back to any of the last 20." Two boards in one sub-tab, two contradictory retention promises.
recommend: Replace the footer with 1704:8309's wording — the last 20 publishes stay restorable — so the panel and its own empty state tell the same story.

finding: Every version row is drawn restorable; the code ships a fourth row state — snapshot pruned, rollback refused — that no board draws.
evidence: PublishHistory.tsx:399 `title={isLive ? "This version is already live" : r.rollbackable ? undefined : "This version's snapshot is no longer stored"}` and :6 "roll back if their payload is still retained (the 20-most-recent keep it)". 949:4474 draws v6/v5/v4/v3 rows with identical affordance and no disabled variant.
recommend: Add the not-rollbackable row to 949:4474 — muted, reason inline — so the pruning rule is visible where it bites rather than only in a tooltip.

finding: Three boards spec a two-tab panel chrome the code deliberately retired, at a drawer width the product does not use.
evidence: 163:2, 163:113 and 1138:4573 all draw header "Versions ✕ / ⟳ Changes / ▣ Saves" at 360px wide. Shipping panel (162:2, 280px) draws "Version History / Saves · Published" plus Milestones|All changes chips. HistoryTab.tsx:3-6 docblock: "view-switcher (Saves / Published) → … Inside Saves, a filter row switches between named milestones and raw recent edits — the old top-level \"Changes\" tab (M1)." Drawer width is fixed: themes/tokens.generated.css:129 `--bk-size-drawer: 280px`.
recommend: Redraw the three at 280px on 162:2's chrome, with All-changes as the selected filter chip rather than a tab; keep the frames, rename to '· all-changes filter'.

finding: The loading state draws only a header — no skeleton rows, no list frame — so it specifies nothing about what the user waits in front of.
evidence: 1138:4573 full text content fetched: "Versions ¶ ✕ ¶ ⟳ Changes ¶ ▣ Saves" and nothing else. Its sibling error state 453:4031 is fully drawn (title, two-line reassurance, Try again). PublishTab's loading peer 778:4238 at least retains section headings.
recommend: Draw the skeleton the list actually renders — 4-5 shimmer rows at the VersionRow height under the real header — so the panel does not appear to have loaded empty.

finding: Three History states are titled "Publish", naming a different panel, and are drawn at a different frame height from every other board in the module.
evidence: 1704:8205 text "Publish ¶ Loading versions…"; 1704:8256 "Publish ¶ Couldn't load publish history"; 1704:8309 "Publish ¶ No published versions yet". All three are 280x812 at x=16000-16760; the rest of History is 280x776 at x≈4560-10640. Shipping header is PanelFrame.Header title="Publish" only in PublishTab.tsx:412; HistoryTab's header reads "Version History" (162:2).
recommend: Retitle the three to "Version History" with the Published view selected, and redraw at 776 so they sit in the History family rather than the Publish one.

finding: A modal asks the user to pick a published version from a list the panel behind it is already showing, with the same rows and the same per-row overflow menu.
evidence: 184:2 text: "Roll back to a published version ¶ v6 · current … v5 … v4 … v3 · approved ¶ Continue ¶ Cancel" — the identical four rows 949:4474 lists ("v6 · current / v5 / v4 / v3 · approved"). 949:4474 already gives each row a "⋯" and a footer button "Roll back to a published version…" wired ON_CLICK to 184:2.
recommend: Drop the picker step: roll back from the row's ⋯ menu straight into the confirm (184:24), which already names the specific version. Keep 184:2 only if a keyboard-only path needs a list dialog.

verdict: UNSURE(needs a product call before it is built)
finding: Backups introduces a third restore-point noun beside Saves and Published, and a Buildrik user has no way to know which of the three to reach for when something breaks.
evidence: 950:4474 draws a 4th tab alongside Changes/Saves/Published with "Automatic backups · Daily at 3:00 AM EST · retain 30 days" and "Backups capture the whole site. Restoring replaces current content." Saves already restores whole-project snapshots (site-version.service.ts:13 MAX_VERSIONS_PER_SITE = 50, `get returns the payload for restore`). The board self-declares "design-ahead · no backend yet".
recommend: Before building, decide whether Backups is a retention policy over Saves rather than a separate object — a "kept nightly" badge on the Saves list would deliver the same safety with one noun instead of three.

screen: History · retention rules across the module
finding: The module states three different retention rules in three places and never reconciles them on any one screen, so "how far back can I go" has no single answer.
evidence: 162:2 footer "50 versions kept. Auto-saves prune oldest first; named ones never prune."; 1704:8309 "roll back to any of the last 20"; 950:4474 "retain 30 days". Code confirms two of them are real and different: site-version.service.ts:13 (50) and publish.service.ts:436 (20).
recommend: State the rule once per sub-tab in the same sentence shape, and drop the module-level implication that one number governs everything.

finding: Both Backups boards wire their Changes tab to the retired two-tab chrome, so the design-ahead surface leads into a design the code has already replaced.
evidence: 950:4474 reactions: `tab/Changes >[ON_CLICK] NODE -> 163:2`, `tab/Saves -> 162:2`, `tab/Published -> 949:4474`; 1156:4620 carries the same four. 163:2 is the retired-chrome board identified in D-E-03.
recommend: Re-point both tab/Changes hotspots at 162:2 with the All-changes chip selected once D-E-03 is redrawn.

screen: History · Saves / Published — row overflow menu
finding: A "⋯" overflow sits on every version row across nine boards and its contents are never drawn anywhere in the module, including the destructive item the API supports.
evidence: "⋯" appears on 4 rows each in 162:2, 163:113, 163:167, 163:220, 163:269 and 949:4474, and on the Backups rows in 950:4474. No board in section 1776:8374 draws an open menu. server/trpc/routers/site-version.ts:47 exposes `delete: protectedProcedure`, and site-version.service.ts:54 notes "the editor mirror fires delete best-effort" — so deleting a save is a real capability with no designed surface.
recommend: Draw the row menu once (Rename, Compare with current, Restore, Delete) and reuse it on both sub-tabs; deleting a named milestone needs its own confirm, since it is the one action here that destroys a restore point.

finding: Version history does earn object status in a site-builder's model — "put it back the way it was" is a top-three anxiety once a site is live — but the 21 screens are carrying two nouns' worth of surface (Saves and Published) plus a speculative third.
evidence: Both halves are backed by shipping code with distinct storage: site-version.service.ts (50 project snapshots, restore) and publish.service.ts:434-459 (20 publish payloads, rollback/redeploy). HistoryTab.tsx renders both through one PanelFrame with a Saves/Published view switcher. Backups (950:4474, 1156:4620) has no backend by its own annotation.
recommend: Keep the module; the excess is not the concept but the duplication inside it — D-E-03 (three stale-chrome boards), D-E-06 (a redundant picker) and D-E-07 (a third noun) account for six of the 21.

screen: Publish · panel (+ publishing / live / failed / Options)
finding: Every Publish board lists a second environment, "Preview · brk-preview.vercel.app", that does not exist — a Buildrik-branded host from the retired hosted model — and the design has already driven a permanently-empty row into the shipping panel.
evidence: "Preview ¶ brk-preview.vercel.app ¶ ›" appears in 641:2652, 784:4250, 784:4326, 784:4403 and 912:4520. Code honours the board and ships the row blank on purpose: usePublishSnapshot.ts returns `preview: { label: "Preview", value: null }` under the comment "Preview deployments are a Vercel concept this editor does not read yet. The row stays — the board draws the pair, and an environment list that hides Preview would say the site has none." Sites deploy into the workspace's own Vercel account (784:4480: "Buildrick deploys into your own Vercel account — we host nothing").
recommend: Cut the Preview row from all five boards and let ENVIRONMENT state the one target that exists; if Vercel preview deployments are wanted later, they arrive as a real value read from the connection, not as a Buildrik-branded placeholder domain.

finding: All three wizard boards print a three-step stepper; the product ships two steps, and Confirm's Back button leads to the step that does not exist.
evidence: 833:4518, 893:4518 and 914:4507 each carry "1. Review ¶ 2. Options ¶ 3. Confirm". PublishWizard.tsx:10-16: "TWO steps, not the three the stepper is drawn with. Board 912:4520 (\"2. Options\") carries its own annotation: design-ahead · no backend yet"; the code renders `{i + 1}. {s === "review" ? "Review" : "Confirm"}` over `type Step = "review" | "confirm"`. 914:4507 reaction: `← Back >[ON_CLICK] NODE -> 912:4520`.
recommend: Redraw the stepper as 1. Review / 2. Confirm on the three shipping boards and re-point Back to 833:4518; leave 912:4520 as the design-ahead spec it declares itself to be, holding the third step until publishInputSchema carries those fields.

finding: Taking a live site down is fully built, hosts its confirm inside the Publish panel, and has no board anywhere in the 14 — the most destructive action in the module is the one with no design.
evidence: packages/editor/src/services/PublishService.ts:239 `unpublishSite`, documented at :234 as "flips the site to DRAFT (publish.service.ts unpublishSite); ADMIN only". PublishTab.tsx:179-183: "unpublishSite was fully built — Vercel teardown included … This panel hosts the ONE confirm; the site menu opens the panel and asks it (UI_UNPUBLISH_REQUEST)", with state `confirmUnpublish` / `unpublishing` at :185-186. server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:428 `unpublish`. No frame in section 1776:8378 mentions unpublish.
recommend: Board the confirm and the in-flight/failed states: it needs to say what stops working (the public URL), that content and history survive, and that only an admin can do it — the same three-fact shape the rollback confirm 184:24 already uses well.

finding: A running publish cannot be stopped from the editor: the board offers no cancel, the panel renders none, and the cancelled outcome the hook can produce has no screen and no renderer.
evidence: 784:4250 text ends at "Building · step 2 of 4 · started 14s ago … Publishing…" — no cancel control. usePublishJob.ts:97 declares `cancel: () => Promise<void>`, :228-231 implements it against `cancelPublishCall`, and :33 declares uiState `"cancelled"` set at :305 — grep for `.cancel()` and for `"cancelled"` across packages/editor/src/editor returns zero non-test callers and zero render sites. The dashboard does offer it: packages/dashboard/components/publish/publish-progress.tsx:35 `trpc.sites.cancelPublish.useMutation`. Server: sites.ts:402.
recommend: Add a Cancel to 784:4250 and a "Publish · cancelled" state saying the live site is unchanged — the same reassurance half 781:4489 and 453:4064 already carry. Without it a user who mis-clicks Publish must watch it finish.

finding: An Export modal is filed inside the Publish section; export and publish are different jobs — one takes the site away, the other makes it live — and it sits 27,000px from the Publish cluster with all its wiring pointing at Export screens.
evidence: 1172:4825 at x=10640, y=53716; every other Publish frame sits y≈25100-26080. Its copy is "Export site as HTML ¶ A .zip with every page, styles inlined, media included — host it anywhere." Reactions leave the section entirely: `-> 1171:4767`, `btn/Cancel -> 642:3401`, `btn/Export as HTML -> 642:3401`.
recommend: Move the frame to the Export family so "Publish · 14 screens" counts 13 publish screens; nothing about the frame itself needs changing.

finding: WITHDRAWN by D-E-33 — see that row. The loading state draws three section headings over empty space and leaves the primary CTA looking live, so the panel reads as a site with nothing to publish rather than a panel still loading.
evidence: 778:4238 full text: "Publish ¶ ENVIRONMENT ¶ SINCE LAST DEPLOY ¶ LAST DEPLOY ¶ Publish to production" — headings and CTA, no values, no skeleton, no disabled treatment on the footer button.
recommend: Skeleton the three section bodies and show the CTA disabled while the snapshot loads; the same fix pattern as D-E-04.

finding: The Preview section contains no board for the preview the product actually ships: all six frames are self-declared not-implemented or design-ahead, while the real preview mode — bound to a chord, with a device switcher and a device bezel — is boarded only outside this section.
evidence: Section 1779:4 frame names: 817:4774 [not-implemented · superseded], 817:4856 [not-implemented], 817:4899 [not-implemented], 817:4950 [design-ahead], 879:6901 [design-ahead], 1157:4593 [design-ahead]. Shipping surface: editor/shell/PreviewOverlay.tsx — "the topbar stays; everything below it is replaced by a clean, sandboxed render … with a single \"Done\" pill to exit", plus "a device row under the topbar and, on a narrow device, the page inside a bezel" (DeviceFramePreview). Bound at useEditorShortcuts.ts:145 — ⌘P emits UI_TOGGLE_PREVIEW. The overlay's docblock cites boards 65:211 and 807:8663, neither of which is in section 1779:4.
recommend: Either move 65:211 / 807:8663 into the Preview section so the module owns its shipping screen, or rename the section to say it holds unbuilt preview concepts only — as it stands the file appears to have designed preview and has not.

finding: The accessibility checker and the performance audit are one job — "is this site good enough to ship" — split into two surfaces, and the audit board already displays the checker's own score.
evidence: 817:4950 renders four score tiles: "91 Performance ¶ 72 Accessibility ¶ 95 Best Practices ¶ 88 SEO". 817:4899 is titled "Accessibility" and opens on "72 ¶ 3 Errors ¶ 5 Warnings ¶ 12 Passed" — the same 72. Both then list fixable issues with per-issue action buttons (817:4899 "Fix contrast / Add alt text"; 817:4950 "Optimize images / Remove unused CSS").
recommend: Make 817:4950 the one audit report and let each score tile drill into its own issue list — 817:4899 becomes the Accessibility tab of that report, and 879:6901's issue-detail pattern serves both.

finding: This is not a screen — it is a written specification of five preview behaviours laid out as a poster, with a fabricated console log standing in for a UI.
evidence: 817:4856 content is five prose paragraphs describing behaviour rather than an interface: "Clicking a link navigates within preview. Back/forward browser buttons work. Invalid links show yellow warning toast: 'Link target not found: /about'", "Missing images show grey placeholder with broken-image icon. External scripts blocked (security)." Its own title is "Preview interaction testing — 5 feedback types" and its only reaction is `-> 52:2` (back to editor). 1080x540, landscape — no other Preview frame is that shape.
recommend: Re-file to the Notes section as the preview behaviour spec it is; the toast and placeholder states it describes should then be boarded as real states on the preview overlay.

finding: The all-clear board reproduces the entire audit screen to change one block; it is the empty state of the recommendations list, not a screen of its own.
evidence: 1157:4593 and 817:4950 carry an identical metrics block ("First Contentful Paint 1.2s ¶ Largest Contentful Paint 2.1s ¶ Total Blocking Time 120ms ¶ Cumulative Layout Shift 0.08 ¶ Speed Index 2.8s ¶ Time to Interactive 3.4s"), identical chrome and identical reactions (`-> 817:5289`, `Frame -> 879:6896`). The only divergence is the score row and "Recommendations ¶ Nothing to fix — every audit passes."
recommend: Keep the frame but rename it to name the part that varies — '· recommendations · empty' — so it reads as one list state rather than a second report.

screen: CmdK · empty / typing / results / no-results / ai-offer / disabled-command
finding: The premise on these six board names is backwards: ⌘K is not unavailable and these are not an alternative design — they are the boards the shipping shell palette was built from, and ⌘⇧P belongs to a different component entirely.
evidence: editor/shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx docblock: "Triggered by Ctrl+K / ⌘+K"; it is opened at StudioHeader.tsx:250-261 `if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") … setCmdOpen((v) => !v)` and rendered at :848. It cites these very boards: :20-21 "board 166:2 shows a short \"Suggested\" head" for `SUGGESTED_COUNT = 5`, and :31-32 "Board 166:58 — a command you cannot run is still worth seeing" for `disabled` / `disabledReason`; `getRecentCommandIds` supplies 166:2's RECENT band. ⌘⇧P opens canvas/controls/CommandPalette via useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:50. Canvas.tsx:404-405 names both: "the shell's ⌘K (CommandPalette.tsx:125,132) and the canvas's own ⌘⇧P (useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:113,121)". Board 1177:4804's own footer agrees — "25 commands · distinct from shell ⌘K".
recommend: Strike "chord unavailable" from all six names — they are the shipped ⌘K palette. The open question is not which chord but whether the product should ship two palettes at all (see D-E-24).

finding: Two unguarded ⌘K listeners are registered at once, so with the Pages tab open the chord opens the shell palette and the page finder together.
evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:250-264 adds `document.addEventListener("keydown", onKey)` calling `preventDefault()` then `setCmdOpen((v) => !v)`. PagesTab.tsx:124-135 adds `window.addEventListener("keydown", handler)` on the same `(e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k"`, also `preventDefault()` then `setPaletteOpen((open) => !open)`. Neither calls `stopPropagation()`, and document precedes window on the bubble path, so both fire. PagesTab is mounted whenever the Pages tab is open.
recommend: One owner for ⌘K. If the merged palette gains a GO-TO band listing pages (166:27 already draws one), the Pages finder is redundant and its listener should go; otherwise scope the Pages handler to the panel and let it stop propagation.

screen: CmdK (166:*) vs Canvas · command palette (1177:4804) — the merge decision
verdict: MERGE-INTO(166:2 content, at 1177:4804's size and grouping, on ⌘K)
finding: Two palettes ship side by side and each holds half the design: the shell ⌘K palette has the states and no catalogue, the canvas ⌘⇧P palette has the catalogue and no states. Neither is complete, and a user has no way to know which chord reaches which commands.
evidence: 166:* supplies three things 1177:4804 has none of — an opening state with RECENT + SUGGESTED bands (166:2), a no-results state with an AI escape hatch (166:45 "Nothing matches 'qqp'. ¶ Ask AI instead ›", 166:51 "That isn't a command — send it to AI? ¶ AI proposes a diff and never writes directly"), and permission-aware disabled rows with reasons (166:58 "Publish · needs approval ¶ Rollback · admin only", annotated "A command you cannot run is still worth seeing — hiding it means the shortcut someone memorised silently vanishes"). 1177:4804 supplies two things 166:* has none of — a grouped catalogue at scale (EDIT / VIEW / INSERT / TOOLS, "25 commands") and a keyboard-hint footer ("↑↓ Navigate ↵ Select Esc Close"). Shipped widths differ from both boards: shell renders `tw:w-140` = 560px (CommandPalette.tsx:388), canvas renders `width: 520` (controls/CommandPalette.tsx:276); the CmdK boards are drawn 640 wide.
recommend: One palette on ⌘K at 520px. Take 1177:4804's category grouping and footer as the frame; fold in 166:2's RECENT/SUGGESTED opening, 166:45+166:51's no-results-to-AI path, and 166:58's disabled-with-reason rows as states of it. Add 166:27's GO TO as a further category rather than a second taxonomy, which also absorbs the Pages finder and frees the collision in D-E-23. Retire the 640 size — it is the only surface in the editor at that width.

finding: The results board organises hits under ACTIONS / GO TO while the shipped canvas palette organises the same command set under EDIT / VIEW / INSERT / TOOLS — two taxonomies for one list, and the merge cannot adopt both.
evidence: 166:27 bands: "ACTIONS ¶ Send for review ¶ Re-send for review ¶ GO TO ¶ Review panel ¶ Versions". 1177:4804 bands: "EDIT ¶ … VIEW ¶ … INSERT ¶ … TOOLS". The shell palette builds its groups from GROUPED_TABS_CONFIG (shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx:13).
recommend: Keep the verb-based categories for commands and add GO TO as one more category for navigation targets — do-something and go-somewhere is a distinction users read instantly, and it survives a 25-row catalogue where a flat ACTIONS band would not.

finding: The typing board and the results board are the same state one keystroke apart; nothing about the interface differs except the query string and the number of hits.
evidence: 166:18 text: "revi ¶ Send for review ⌘⇧R ¶ Review panel R". 166:27 text: "review ¶ ACTIONS ¶ Send for review ⌘⇧R ¶ Re-send for review ¶ GO TO ¶ Review panel R ¶ Versions ⌘⌥V". Same chrome, same rows, same reactions back to 52:2; 166:18 is 166:27 with the bands not yet shown.
recommend: Keep one filtered-results board. If the intent was to spec that bands appear only past a hit threshold, say so in an annotation on 166:27 rather than spending a frame on it.

finding: A third command palette ships — the Pages go-to-page finder — and has no board in this section or any other, which is how its chord collision reached production unnoticed.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/pages/components/PageCommandPalette.tsx, imported at PagesTab.tsx:18 and opened by the ⌘K handler at PagesTab.tsx:124-135. Section 1779:3 contains seven frames, six for the shell palette and one for the canvas palette; none names pages. Four palette components exist in code (chrome-ui/CommandPalette.tsx, shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx, canvas/controls/CommandPalette.tsx, PageCommandPalette.tsx) against two boarded designs.
recommend: Board it or delete it. The D-E-24 merge makes deletion the better answer — a GO TO band that lists pages does this job inside the one palette, on one chord.

finding: The one board in the module that states the hosting model correctly does it in a single sentence, and it is the model every other Publish board contradicts by drawing a Buildrik preview host.
evidence: 784:4480 text in full: "Publish ¶ Connect Vercel to publish. ¶ Buildrick deploys into your own Vercel account — we host nothing. ¶ Connect Vercel" — shipped verbatim at PublishTab.tsx:425-429. Contrast the ENVIRONMENT block cited in D-E-12.
recommend: Use this sentence as the module's anchor; when D-E-12 is fixed, the ENVIRONMENT block should read as the same product this screen describes.

finding: Every headline number on the audit report is invisible — the four scores are painted in the exact hex of the disc behind them, and the four savings badges are near-identical green-on-green.
evidence: Measured fills: TEXT "91" #0e9f6e on ELLIPSE #0e9f6e; "95" and "88" likewise; TEXT "72" #c27803 on ELLIPSE #c27803 — contrast 1.00:1, the same colour. Savings badges: TEXT "Save ~1.2s LCP" #269966 on FRAME #0e9f6e — computed contrast 1.06:1 (WCAG AA needs 4.5:1). All eight nodes are visible:true, opacity 1, so this is the drawn design, not a hidden layer. Screenshot confirms: four solid discs with no numbers and four solid green pills with no text.
recommend: White text on the score discs and a pale tint behind the savings badges. This is the accessibility audit screen — it currently fails the check it reports on. 1157:4593 draws the same four tiles; it was not separately measured.

screen: History · Saves / Published — view switcher header
finding: The active-tab underline is drawn straight through the tab's own helper text, so on every History board the selected tab's subtitle reads as struck out.
evidence: Measured on 162:2: "View switcher" frame y44 h40 (bottom 84); TEXT "Named milestones" y76 h13 (bottom 89) — 5px past its own container; RECTANGLE "active underline" y82 h2, landing inside the 76-89 text band at roughly its baseline. Same geometry on 949:4474 (helper y75-88, underline y82-84). On 162:2 the next block, "Saves filter", starts at y84, overlapping the helper's last 5px as well. Visible in both screenshots.
recommend: Give the switcher enough height for two lines (48-52px) and move the underline to the frame's true bottom edge, below the helper text — or drop the helper line, which is the cheaper fix since Saves/Published are self-explanatory. Shared header: 7 History boards inherit it, of which 2 were measured.

finding: The footer sentence is a fixed 328px text box inside a 280px panel with truncation disabled, so on both sub-tabs the rule about what gets kept is cut off mid-sentence.
evidence: Measured on 162:2: TEXT "50 versions kept. Auto-saves prune oldest first; named ones never prune." spans L16 to R344 in a 280px frame — 64px past the right edge; textTruncation=DISABLED, textAutoResize=NONE. Same box on 949:4474 for "Every publish is restorable. Rolling back redeploys that version." Screenshots show both clipping — 162:2 ends "…first; nam", 949:4474 ends "…Rolling back redeploys". Drawer width is fixed at 280 (tokens.generated.css:129).
recommend: Set the text box to the panel's content width and let it wrap to two or three lines — there is ample vertical room. Confirms and sharpens D-E-01: the sentence that overpromises restorability is also the one the user never finishes reading.

finding: All four row overflow menus on the Published tab are positioned outside the panel and do not render — leftovers from the 360px layout that the 280px redraw did not bring back in.
evidence: Measured: the four "⋯" TEXT nodes on 949:4474 sit at L320-R331 in a 280px frame — 40px beyond the right edge. The same glyph on 162:2 sits correctly at L216-R227. The screenshot of 949:4474 shows timestamps at the right edge and no overflow affordance on any row; 162:2's render shows all four.
recommend: Move the four nodes to x216 to match 162:2. This is the concrete instance of D-E-10 — on the Published tab the row menu is not merely undrawn, it is drawn off-canvas, so a reviewer reading the board sees no per-row actions at all.

finding: Withdraws D-E-17's primary claim: I reported that 778:4238 draws section headings over empty space with no skeleton. It does draw skeletons — the screenshot shows shimmer bars under all three headings.
evidence: Screenshot of 778:4238 shows grey placeholder bars beneath ENVIRONMENT (2 rows), SINCE LAST DEPLOY (4 rows) and LAST DEPLOY (1 row). My original evidence was a text-node dump, which returns only TEXT nodes and therefore could not see rectangle skeletons — the finding was an artifact of the instrument, not a defect in the board.
recommend: Disregard D-E-17. The surviving half of it — the CTA treatment — is re-filed as D-E-34 on its own evidence.

finding: While the panel is still loading, the primary action renders as a fully enabled accent button, so the one control that ships a site to the public is live before the panel knows what would go out.
evidence: Screenshot of 778:4238: every content region is skeletonised, and the pinned footer button "Publish to production" is drawn in full accent blue with white label — visually identical to the same button on the loaded panel 641:2652. No disabled, muted or spinner treatment.
recommend: Draw the CTA disabled while the snapshot loads. The wizard behind it re-runs its own checks, so this is a clarity fix rather than a safety hole — but a live-looking publish button over an unknown payload is the wrong first impression on this panel.

finding: The empty state tells the user to publish the site and gives them nothing to press, leaving roughly 600px of blank panel under a two-line message.
evidence: Screenshot of 1704:8309: title "No published versions yet" and body "Publish this site and each version shows up here — you can roll back to any of the last 20." occupy the top ~140px of an 812px frame; the remainder is empty and there is no button. Its sibling loading state 778:4238 pins a "Publish to production" CTA at the bottom, and the populated tab 949:4474 pins "Roll back to a published version…" in the same slot.
recommend: Pin a "Publish this site" button in the footer slot the other two boards already use, and lift the message toward optical centre. An empty state that names the action should carry it.

finding: The CmdK boards give their group labels a full-width filled bar that outweighs the commands beneath it, and hold a fixed height that leaves a large void on short result sets.

finding: An internal spec note sits in the palette footer styled exactly like the real keyboard hints next to it, so a literal build would ship it as product copy.
evidence: Screenshot of 1177:4804: the footer reads "↑↓ Navigate  ↵ Select  Esc Close" on the left and "25 commands · distinct from shell ⌘K" on the right, both in the same muted grey at the same size. The right-hand string is an authoring annotation — it describes the board's relationship to another board, and "distinct from shell ⌘K" is meaningless to a user.
recommend: Move it to a Figma comment or a note layer outside the frame. A count of available commands could legitimately stay; the comparison to another palette cannot.

finding: The one named milestone in the list is the only row that shows no name — its title line is a bare flag glyph while every auto-save row carries a label.
evidence: Screenshot of 162:2, third list row: title line renders as "⚑" alone, with "Ali · 8 changes" as the meta line and 15:42 at the right. The other three rows read "Auto-save" over "3 changes" / "1 change" / "2 changes". Text dump agrees: "⚑ ¶ Ali · 8 changes ¶ 15:42 ¶ ⋯". Named versions are the ones users search for — the panel's own search placeholder is "Search saves…" and its filter chip is "Milestones".
recommend: Draw the milestone name beside the flag. As it stands the board specifies that naming a version hides its name, which inverts the feature.
